instruction.text: Draw a line between the Earth and the Moon to learn the distance between them.

feedback.end: The Moon is approximately <mat>380000</mat> kilometres away from Earth. That is equal to a distance of 30 Earths lined up next to each other!

atoms.b: A moon is a celestial body that ((++orbits turns_into)) a planet.
Other planets can also have moons. Mars has 2 moons, and Saturn has 146 — the ((++most least)) in the solar system!
Earth, however, has just one, which is why we call it the ((++Moon moon)).
atoms.sound: Earth, however, has just one, which is why we call it 'thee' Moon.

instruction.text: Is the Moon more visible during the day or at night?

atoms.b: The Moon is illuminated by ((++the_Sun Venus)), which makes it ((++visible invisible)) to us — particularly at night!

As the Moon orbits the ((++Earth Sun)), and simultaneously rotates on its axis, we can only see its ((++illuminated dark)) parts, while the rest is hidden in the shadows. This creates the different phases of the Moon.
During a ((++full half)) moon, the entire face of the Moon is visible from Earth, while during a ((++new_moon crescent_moon)), the Moon is completely hidden from view.
